title: ASSIGNMENT – 5
subtitle: Simulation of Consistent Hashing over MongoDB (Spring Boot)
name: Srikrishna O S

sections.heading: AIM
sections.paragraph: To implement consistent hashing using Spring Boot and MongoDB, distributing Student records across three storage nodes (Docker containers) via a hash ring with virtual nodes. The experiment demonstrates that adding or removing a node only re-routes a small fraction of keys, unlike modulo hashing which reshuffles all records.

rows: Built ConsistentHashRing using MD5 hash and TreeMap for sorted positions
Ring operational with 3 nodes and 3 virtual nodes each
Docker Compose launched mongo-node1 (27017), node2 (27018), node3 (27019)
POST /students with rollNo, name, department, year
Records distributed across nodes per hash ring mapping
Initial distribution e.g. node1: 5, node2: 4, node3: 6
Only a small fraction of records moved; rest untouched
That node's records relocated; other nodes' data untouched

sections.heading: ANALYSIS
sections.paragraph: Consistent hashing maps both keys and nodes onto a circular hash ring (0 to 2^32-1 using MD5). Each physical node gets virtual nodes (default 3) for even distribution. Student records (identified by rollNo) are assigned to the first node clockwise from their hash position. Adding a node only claims the slice between it and its clockwise predecessor — all other keys stay put. Removing a node only reassigns its own slice. This contrasts with modulo hashing (`hash(key) % N`), where changing N reshuffles every key's bucket. The experiment confirms the core benefit: minimal data movement during scale-out/scale-in.
